title: DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2 Lands, and It Can Delegate to Codex and Claude
summary: DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2 launches with delegation to Codex and Claude
detailed: DeepSeek released DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1 on November 4, 2026, featuring new multi-language support, Git worktrees, and an experimental plugin that delegates tasks to Codex and Claude.

As of November 7, 2026, the open-source repository reached 275,571 stars and 33,699 forks, with the program recording 1.54 million daily active users relying on the official DeepSeek API as of November 4.
The free MIT-licensed tool runs locally from the terminal via Node.js and acts as an open alternative to Claude Code and Codex.
This matters because a competing coding agent platform is integrating direct collaboration with alternative industry tools, expanding its ecosystem functionality.
sentences: DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1, published on November 4, 2026, is the first release candidate in the 0.2.2 series of the open source program DeepSeek uses to put its models to work as agents on the user's own computer.
It brings the interface to six more languages, Git worktrees and an experimental plugin that hands tasks off to Codex and Claude.
The Hangzhou-based company behind the V4 models calls the harness the scaffolding that surrounds the model.
It reads a project's files, runs commands, asks permission before acting and organizes the work into sessions.
The command is called dsh , the license is MIT, and you start it with npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web , which opens the interface in the browser.
It is the open alternative to Claude Code and Codex.
We have followed it from the first release to the 200,000 stars .
The project isn't slowing down.
The repository, created on August 13, has 275,571 stars and 33,699 forks as of November 7, 2026 (on October 28, in our piece on DS Bot , the stars were above 264,000).
Releases, after all, are shipping at construction-site speed, with five landing between October 28 and November 4.
On the user side, the figures released by the Harness team are picked up by TechNode , which cites IT Home.
As of November 4 the program had 1.54 million daily active users, counted only among those using it with the official DeepSeek API.
Third-party plugins number around 35,000, and about 60% of active users have built or installed at least one.
DeepSeek, for its part, says it wants to build an official plugin marketplace, with token incentives for creators.
For now it is only a plan, with no amounts.
DeepSeek Harness is free (MIT license) and starts from the terminal with npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web .
You need Node.js (version 24.9 or later from the 0.2.2 series on) and a model to configure.
It is still a developer preview, and the rc.1 candidate is on the releases page.
The rc tag stands for release candidate, the build the authors put forward as the basis for the stable version.
The README , however, calls the whole project a developer preview and warns in capital letters that breaking changes are coming.
The last eight published releases are all marked as pre-releases.
The official notes list thirteen new features, arriving after the alpha.2 of October 28 and the alpha.3 of November 3 .
The most concrete ones touch everyday use.
You can quote a piece of the chat inside the input box, copy an entire session as Markdown and keep all of the assistant's replies visible even when the work steps are collapsed.
There is a single context menu for sessions, workspaces and the sidebar, while file previews get a folder tree that stays in view.
The layout for phones and tablets has been reworked, on-screen keyboard included.
The plugin manager, for its part, learns to update third-party packages and, if a hot update fails, tries to roll back to the previous version.
It is the feature you notice least and that matters most, because an ecosystem of independent extensions now lives around DeepSeek Harness, like the DS Bot mentioned above.
A Git worktree is a second working copy of the same repository, with its own branch and its own folder.
For a coding agent, it keeps each session's changes separate from the main project, so several sessions can run in parallel without stepping on each other.
The experimental «Change requests and worktrees» plugin (change requests and worktrees) runs each session in its own worktree.
It shows local diffs and pull request diffs through a searchable file tree, with file-by-file navigation.
It lets you quote lines of code and comments to the model.
It also tracks the status of automated checks and reviews.
It absorbs the separate «Git worktrees» plugin, so anyone who had enabled it has to remove @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-worktree from dsh.profile.bundles by hand.
The other two experimental plugins are more peripheral.
One shows, for each turn and step, statistics on context, cache, model and tool timings, while the other offers cards under the replies for enabling official plugins or creating custom pages.
The change that will make the most noise is a different one.
The experimental subagent_oar plugin, introduced with alpha.2, lets you hand independent tasks to the Codex or Claude command line installed on the same machine.
A program built to compete with Codex and Claude Code is, in effect, learning to use them as collaborators.
A curious way to make alliances.
The notes don't explain how accounts, costs and permissions for those two CLIs (command-line interfaces) are handled.
They also don't say whether the delegated task comes back with the same work trace you see for internal subagents.
The only way to find out is to try it.
It remains, in any case, a signal of how DeepSeek sees its own product, as more of a control room than a rival to beat.

On the self-improving agent front, the same trend shows up in how to improve an agent without retraining the model and in the numbers of the Harness Leaderboard , where changing only the harness moves the score by 24 points.
The least flashy part of the candidate is the most delicate.
By default, the checks that blocked writing to a file the agent had never read, or that someone else had changed in the meantime, are now turned off.

The sandbox limits (the isolated area where the agent can operate) and the Review screen, where changes are visible before you accept them, remain; anyone who wants the old checks can restore them through the profile's observation policy.
In the same direction goes apply_patch , off by default, which creates, edits, deletes and moves multiple files in a single call, with the changes available in Review.
Web Fetch (the tool the agent uses to download web pages) can now reach non-public addresses, useful behind a proxy or on an internal network.
The notes warn that whoever installs it must restrict network access on their own.
Anyone running shared machines should factor that in before upgrading, bearing in mind that the project's safety notice rules out an audit and recommends disposable environments.
Since alpha.2, the minimum requirement is Node.js 24.9 .
The notes ask you to update the runtime before updating DeepSeek Harness.
For plugin authors, the migration work is not small.
The developer-facing additions also include a VM Script mode with top-level await and Session APIs that read snapshots and continuously follow the event log.
The candidate adds text and configuration for Japanese, Spanish, French, German, Russian and Brazilian Portuguese.
The upload limit for each image rises to 50 MiB, and WebSocket compression for remote connections is on by default, useful for long histories (you turn it off with websocketCompression ).
0.2.2-rc.1 is marked as a pre-release on GitHub, like the last eight.
